location: Feed picture click in Program mode
issue: One click on a feed picture is specified as both 'cut Program to this feed' and 'focus this tile'. The focused tile is the target of ⌃⌥F/⌃⌥C and the tools, so adjusting monitoring on the NEXT feed cuts it on air.
evidence: main-expanded legend 2: 'Click a picture or press ⌃1/⌃2 to cut'. monitor-tools keyboard card: 'Click a tile to focus it (blue ring). Shortcuts act on the focused tile only, as today.' MonitorWorkspaceShell.swift: TapGesture().onEnded { focusedTile = index }.
scenario: T4: mid-meeting the user clicks Feed 2 to turn on zebra before cutting, and Zoom immediately cuts to Feed 2 with an unchecked frame.
recommendation: Picture click only focuses or selects. Cuts come only from explicit cut controls: toolbar cut buttons, cut bar, ⌃1–⌃4, dropdown thumbnails, and a dedicated 'Cut' pill on non-air pictures.
alternatives: Double-click a picture to cut
⌥-click to cut, with a hint in the hover toolbar
Click arms the cut (green 'NEXT') and a second click or Return takes it, like a switcher's preview/program

issue: The live window has no visible Start or Stop control for a feed. The expanded strip header has only a status badge and ⋯; the r3 toolbar dropped Start/Stop; the ⋯ popover footer has Rename/Diagnostics/Remove only. Starting and stopping live only in Feed ▸ ⌘↩ and the dropdown. Only the 'Feed stopped' state (states page) shows a Start Feed button.
evidence: r3.js strip(expanded) header: name, cam, 'Live · fmt' badge, ⋯ button. r3.js toolbar(): title, cuts, layout, collapse, record; no Start/Stop. main-collapsed ⋯ footer: Rename…, Diagnostics…, Remove Camera.
scenario: T5/T2: after a recording session the user wants to stop Feed 2's capture to free the device or GPU and can't find how without the menu.
recommendation: Put a Start/Stop Feed control in each strip header (expanded) and in the collapsed row's hover controls. In automatic mode show 'Automatic' plus Retry instead.
alternatives: Make the 'Live · 2160p59.94' badge a pop-up button with Stop Feed / Restart
A toolbar Start/Stop that acts on the selected feed, labelled with its name

issue: Stopping a feed silently ends that feed's recording, but no design says so or asks first. ⌘↩ is a single keystroke and the Feed menu or dropdown 'Stop Feed' sits above the recording rows.
evidence: AppModel.stop(): manuallyStoppedFeeds.insert…; feedCoordinator.stop(selectedFeedID); recordingModel.stop(feedID: selectedFeedID). menubar (b)/(g) 'Stop Feed ⌘↩' with 'Stop Recording 12:31' listed separately below.
scenario: T2: the user wants to briefly stop the camera feed (e.g. to change input) during a backup take and ends the backup recording without realising.
recommendation: When the feed is recording, label it 'Stop Feed and Recording…' and ask once ('Feed 1 is recording 38:12. Stopping the feed ends the take.' [Keep Recording] [Stop Both]). Same in the strip control from L1-02.
alternatives: Disable Stop Feed while recording with 'Stop the recording first'
Make ⌘↩ require the window to be frontmost and never act from the dropdown

issue: In Program mode the dropdown offers 'Stop Feeds', plural, implying every source stops. The code's stop() stops only the selected feed (and its recording); the other headless Program sources and their recordings keep running.
evidence: menubar.html Program dropdown row 'Stop Feeds' ⌘↩. AppModel.stop() only calls feedCoordinator.stop(selectedFeedID) and recordingModel.stop(feedID: selectedFeedID); startFeed() in Program mode starts every enabled source.
scenario: T4 after a two-camera meeting: the user presses Stop Feeds, sees Feed 1 stop, and leaves. Feed 2 keeps capturing and recording to the drive.
recommendation: Decide the model. Either 'Stop All Feeds' truly stops all sources (a model change, matching how Program starts all), or label it 'Stop Feed 1' and show the other sources still running. Program-mode start/stop should be symmetric.
alternatives: Separate rows: 'Stop Feed 1' and 'Stop All Feeds'
End Meeting command: stop all feeds and recordings with one confirmation

location: Effect toggles while Zoom is live (strip chips, ⋯ popover, dropdown Effects submenu)
issue: Changing Downscale, Color or Frame rate changes the published format. The producer drains and renegotiates the camera transport, which can blank or hiccup Zoom. No design warns about this, and the existing 'Applying change…' feedback state is gone. A LUT toggle doesn't change the format and is safe, but nothing tells the two apart.
evidence: README: 'The producer stops and drains its camera transport before negotiating a changed output format, then resumes delivery.' Current AppliedPipelineState shows 'Applying change…'. 'Applying' appears on no r3 page. The Effects submenu (single/menubar) lists all four toggles identically.
scenario: T3: during a meeting the user unticks '3 · Color 4:2:0' to test 10-bit and Zoom freezes or blacks for a moment in front of the call.
recommendation: Mark format-changing effects (2, 3, 4) with 'Changes Zoom's format · brief interruption' when a consumer is active, ask before applying while ON AIR, and restore an 'Applying change…' transitional state on the strip chips and result line. Keep the LUT toggle instant.
alternatives: Defer format changes while ON AIR: 'Apply when Zoom stops using the camera'
Lock format-changing effects while the camera is in use and show why

location: Per-feed effect chips in Program mode
issue: Strips present each feed's output effects as independent, but Program's transport contract is recomputed from whichever feed is on air at each applied cut. Feeds with different format settings (or LUT on vs off) can make every cut reconfigure the Program camera. Nothing shows the Program output format or flags a mismatch.
evidence: AppModel feedCoordinator.onProgramCutApplied → reconcileProgramTransportDemand(); programContract(configuration: producer's configuration…). main-expanded: Feed 1 fx [LUT,1080p,4:2:0], Feed 2 [1080p,4:2:0], with no Program format shown.
scenario: T4: Feed 2 is set to 4:2:2 10-bit (Color off). Every Auto cut to Feed 2 renegotiates Zoom's camera format, producing repeated glitches the user can't trace.
recommendation: Show 'Program output: 1080p 29.97 · 4:2:0' in the sidebar Output section, and flag strips whose output format differs ('Differs from Program: cuts may interrupt'). Consider a single Program format that sources conform to.
alternatives: Force matching format effects across Program sources (lock 2–4 to Program)
Warn once when entering Program mode with mismatched feeds

location: After the meeting: Zoom closes while a backup take is running
issue: Today, recording counts as demand, so when Zoom closes the feed and the backup take keep running indefinitely. No page designs this 'meeting ended, still recording' state. Only the proposed NEW auto-stop toggle covers it.
evidence: AppModel.reconcileAutomaticFeed(): demand(camera || programRequested || recording); case .stop: guard …, !recording. No page contains 'meeting ended', 'Zoom closed' or an equivalent. menubar/settings show 'Stop when the last camera app closes' as NEW only.
scenario: T2: the user ends the Zoom call and closes the laptop lid or walks away. The take keeps filling the 8TB drive for hours and the next meeting's backup lands in the same huge file.
recommendation: Design a post-meeting state: an orange banner in the dropdown and window plus a notification, 'Zoom stopped using Ultracam · Feed 1 still recording 1:02:31' [Stop Recording] [Keep Recording]. Make 'Stop when the last camera app closes' default-on when 'Record with camera apps' is on.
alternatives: Auto-stop after N minutes without a consumer (setting)
Menu bar icon pulses or turns orange when recording with no consumer

location: Strip after Stop / sidebar Recent Takes
issue: There's no post-take state. After Stop, the strip goes back to 'Ready', with no 'Saved · file name · duration · Show in Finder'. Recent Takes rows have no reveal action (round 2 had one), so 'find the files' needs the dropdown or Record menu 'Show Recordings in Finder', which opens a folder, not the take. The current app keeps final take statistics visible until the next take.
evidence: r3.js sidebar() take row: icon + name only, no button. states expanded 'Ready' strip has no last-take line. README: 'Final take statistics remain visible until the next take.'
scenario: T5: after recording a 40-minute interview on two cameras, the user wants to check both files and drag them into an editor. They must open the folder and hunt by timestamp.
recommendation: Add a 'Saved' strip state ('Saved · Feed 1_2026-10-20_09-41-03_001.mov · 38:12 · 56 GB · 0 dropped' [Show in Finder] [Quick Look]) that persists until the next take. Give Recent Takes rows reveal-on-hover and drag-out.
alternatives: A one-line 'Last take' in the collapsed strip
Notification on finalize with a Show action

location: Rename… / Add Camera while anything is running
issue: Rename (⋯ footer, Feed menu 'Rename Feed 1…') and the sidebar '+' are drawn enabled during a live, recording session. The model only allows rename, add, remove and output-mode changes when every source is stopped and nothing is recording, so T8 'rename one camera without touching the other' fails silently.
evidence: AppModel.renameFeed/addFeed guard canEditFeedTopology; FeedLifecycleDemandPolicy.canEditTopology = !loading && !sourceActive && !recordingActive. main-collapsed ⋯ footer 'Rename…' enabled; app-menus row('Rename Feed 1…') enabled; r3.js sidebar plus icon not disabled. Only app-menus 'Add Camera · stop to change' is disabled.
scenario: T8: during a take the user tries to rename 'Feed 2' to 'B-cam'. Nothing happens, or the field reverts.
recommendation: Disable with the reason everywhere ('Stop all feeds and recordings to rename'), or better, relax the model so renaming is metadata-only (it affects the next take's folder and file names and the virtual camera name).
alternatives: Allow rename while running but defer applying it until feeds stop, with a 'pending' badge

location: Going from one camera to two-camera switching (Output mode) / first Zoom setup
issue: Moving to Program is a hidden, multi-step flow: stop everything, + Add Camera, choose its input in ⋯, switch Output mode in Settings or the Program menu (locked while running), then choose a DIFFERENT camera in Zoom ('Ultracam · Program' instead of 'Ultracam · Feed 1'). No page guides it or tells the user to re-pick the camera in Zoom. The onboarding card also never says which camera name to choose in Zoom.
evidence: VirtualCameraRegistryPublishing: Separate mode publishes 'Ultracam · <feed>', Program publishes 'Ultracam · Program'. settings Camera pane lists names without a call to action. app-menus Program ▸ Output Mode is disabled ('change while stopped'). states first-launch steps: install → input → LUT → folder, with no Zoom step.
scenario: T4: the user switches to Program for a two-camera call. Zoom keeps showing 'Ultracam · Feed 1' (now no longer published), the call shows black, and the user doesn't know why.
recommendation: Add a guided 'Set Up Switching…' sheet (add camera → input → mode) and, after any mode change or first install, a persistent banner: 'In Zoom › Video, choose Ultracam · Program'. Add that as the last onboarding step.
alternatives: Keep a stable 'Ultracam' camera name in both modes (a model change) so Zoom never needs re-selecting
A status bar Output popover hint when the expected camera has no consumer for 30 s

location: First run: Install Camera → System Settings approval
issue: No state covers the gap between 'Install Camera' and the user approving the extension in System Settings (the installer has a pending state), or an approval that's declined or ignored. The onboarding step goes from an Install button straight to done.
evidence: ExtensionInstaller has `pending` and a status text; the current UI disables Install/Remove while pending. states first-launch step 1 'Install the Ultracam camera … Approve …' shows only an Install button; settings Camera shows only installed or not.
scenario: T1: the user clicks Install, the macOS approval prompt is dismissed or hidden behind windows, and Ultracam gives no hint what to do next. Zoom has no camera.
recommendation: Design 'Waiting for approval' (spinner, 'Approve Ultracam Camera in System Settings › General › Login Items & Extensions › Camera Extensions' [Open System Settings]), 'Approval needed again', and 'Installed: reopen Zoom's camera menu' states, both in onboarding and in sidebar Output.
alternatives: A short animated how-to in the onboarding card

location: Overriding Auto during a Program meeting
issue: A manual cut with Auto on is passed to the director as a manual override, so Auto keeps running and may cut away again after the minimum shot. No page explains this or offers a 'Hold' that pauses Auto without turning it off, although NaturalTalkingHeadSettings.manualHold exists and the director honours it. The only way to keep a shot is to turn Auto off and remember to turn it back on.
evidence: AppModel.requestProgramCut → autoSwitcherBridge.manualOverride(…). director.rs: `if self.config.manual_hold { return None; }`. AppSettingsStore.manualHold (not shown in r3 settings, which the agent judged runtime state). No page contains 'Hold'.
scenario: T4: the guest starts a long answer and the user cuts to Feed 2 to stay on them. Twenty seconds later Auto cuts back to the host mid-sentence.
recommendation: Add 'Hold' (toggle, e.g. ⌃⌥H) next to Auto in the toolbar cut group, cut bar and dropdown, mapped to manualHold. After a manual cut, show the shot timer state 'Manual cut · Auto may cut after 10 s'.
alternatives: Manual cut auto-holds for N seconds (setting)
Long-press a cut button to cut and hold

location: Effect chips in the channel strip
issue: The LUT / 1080p / 4:2:0 / 29.97 chips read as status badges. Nothing shows they're toggles (no hover or pressed affordance, no tooltip), so T3 'turn the LUT off' from the window isn't discoverable. The documented paths are the ⋯ popover or the dropdown submenu.
evidence: r3.js fxChips(): plain spans styled as badges. spec §4 says 'effect chips = Toggle(.button)', but nothing on the pages communicates it.
scenario: T3: mid-meeting the user looks at the strip to turn the LUT off, doesn't recognise the chip as a button, and opens Settings instead.
recommendation: Render chips as a segmented row of toggle buttons with hover, pressed and tooltip states ('LUT on: click to bypass the LUT'), or replace them with a compact 'Effects ▾' pop-up button listing the four ordered toggles.
alternatives: Keep the chips as status only and add an 'Effects' button beside them

issue: The toolbar's primary recording control shows only '■ 12:31 · 2', with no verb. While recording it's Stop All, at rest presumably Record All, but the label never says which, and it sits beside the per-strip 'Stop' (recording) and 'Pause'.
evidence:
r3.js toolbar(): `
${ic('stop')}${recLabel}
`, with recLabel '12:31 · 2'. standalone wrote 'Stop All · 12:31' locally.
scenario: T5: at the end of a session the user isn't sure whether the red pill stops both cameras or only the focused one, and stops the cameras one by one in the strips.
recommendation: Always include the verb and scope: 'Record All' at rest, 'Stop All · 12:31 · 2' while recording (as standalone.html does). The tooltip lists which feeds are affected.
alternatives: A split button: main = Stop All, menu = per-feed stop/pause

location: Automatic mode: opening the window before a meeting
issue: A visible preview counts as demand in automatic mode, so opening the main window to check framing starts capture and GPU work. The 'Automatic mode waiting / Waiting for a camera app' picture card can't occur in a visible main window with preview on. The menubar agent handled this for the dropdown only ('Show Live Preview').
evidence: README: 'Start for a camera app or a visible preview.' AppModel.reconcileAutomaticFeed(): policy.previewDemand(legacyVisible || monitorDemand…). states §3 'Automatic mode waiting' card shows a main-window picture placeholder.
scenario: T2: the user opens Ultracam an hour before the meeting to check settings. The feed starts and stays running (GPU and fans) until they hide the preview or close the window.
recommendation: Either show the waiting placeholder with an explicit 'Show Live Preview (starts the feed)' button in the window too, matching the dropdown, or keep the demand rule and say so on the picture: 'Preview started the feed · it stops when you close the window'.
alternatives: Let the main window open in a 'waiting' layout until the user asks for preview

location: Record All when some feeds aren't running
issue: Recording needs a running feed ('Start this feed before recording it'). Record All with one feed stopped or without signal records only part of the session, and no page shows what Record All will actually include before or after pressing it.
evidence: RecordingModel: 'Start this feed before recording it. Only an active source feed can produce media.' four-up: Feed 3 'No HDMI signal' with Record disabled; the toolbar shows '12:31 · 3' with no indication that Feed 3 is excluded.
scenario: T5: the user presses Record All for a three-camera interview without noticing Feed 3 has no signal, and loses the third angle.
recommendation: Label it with scope ('Record All · 2 of 3 ready') and, when pressed with an unready feed, flag it: an orange 'Feed 3 not recording · no signal' in the status bar and the strip, plus an optional confirmation.
alternatives: Record All arms unready feeds and starts them automatically when their signal arrives

evidence: main-expanded legend 2 (click to cut) plus monitor-tools 'Click a tile to focus it'; MonitorWorkspaceShell TapGesture focuses the tile. See L1-01.

The dropdown labels 'Processing · Feed 1' (menubar a) and the Feed menu header says 'acts on Feed 1', but the window shows no selection; ⇧⌘B from the window has no visible target. selectFeed() also rebinds the main native preview.
Refined: only format-changing effects (Downscale, Color, Frame rate) renegotiate; LUT doesn't. 'Applying change…' is gone from r3. In Program mode cuts can renegotiate too (L1-06). See L1-05.
r3 removed the toolbar feed Stop, so the main ambiguity is the verb-less toolbar record button vs strip Stop/Pause (L1-14) and Stop Feed silently ending takes (L1-03).
Program start starts all sources but stop() stops only the selected feed; the dropdown says 'Stop Feeds'. See L1-04.

Strip 'Stop' sits directly right of 'Pause' with the same size and style (main-expanded, standalone). A conventional recorder pattern, but no undo, and a mis-click ends the backup take. Severity left to L2.

T9 is completable from the dropdown (start, effects, record, cut, auto, recover via Record menu), but Program dropdown (a) is ~790 pt tall plus a submenu; marginal on 1440×900 laptops. Detail left to L4/L5.
